items.title: One Patient, Multiple Decisions: Interprofessional Care In The Malaysian Health Care System — MHSA
items.summary: The Malaysian Healthcare Students Alliance (MHSA) warns that professional hierarchies and poor communication among health care workers can compromise patient safety. The alliance calls for stronger collaboration across disciplines to improve patient care. The post One Patient, Multiple Decisions: Interprofessional Care In The Malaysian Health Care System — MHSA appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: Malaysia Needs MHTC-Like Agency To Coordinate Long-Term Care
items.summary: Malaysia needs a central agency to prepare for its rapidly ageing population, but aged care responsibilities remain fragmented across ministries, with KPWKM classified as a “Category C” ministry and lacking the clout to lead a national response. The post Malaysia Needs MHTC-Like Agency To Coordinate Long-Term Care appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: An Open Letter To The Sabah Chief Minister: Sarawak Is Investing In Its Future Doctors, But Why Is Sabah Still Falling Behind? — An Exhausted Doctor
items.summary: A doctor practising in Sabah wants the state government to match Sarawak’s investment in local medical graduates, calling for scholarships and better rural infrastructure, housing and financial incentives to stem the exodus of doctors. The post An Open Letter To The Sabah Chief Minister: Sarawak Is Investing In Its Future Doctors, But Why Is Sabah Still Falling Behind? — An Exhausted Doctor appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: What Is The Status Of Our NG-999? — Dr Sarah Shaikh Abdul Karim
items.summary: One year after NG-999's rollout, retreating to 21 fragmented hospital call centres wastes scarce clinical manpower and stalls emergency dispatch reform. The post What Is The Status Of Our NG-999? — Dr Sarah Shaikh Abdul Karim appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: Doctors Have A Voice On Poisons Board, But How Much Weight Does It Carry? — Dr Pearl Leong
items.summary: Dr Pearl Leong questions the Poisons Board’s nicotine exemption U-turn. Business representatives hold four of 12 seats, against three for medical representatives, but “without individual voting records”, doctors cannot be said to have been outvoted. The post Doctors Have A Voice On Poisons Board, But How Much Weight Does It Carry? — Dr Pearl Leong appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: Insurers Must Expand GP Coverage To Curb Rising Private Health Care Costs — PMPASKL
items.summary: PMPASKL backs APHM’s warning that patients bypassing GPs for routine illnesses are contributing to rising private health care costs. It urges insurers and TPAs to expand outpatient GP coverage to curb unnecessary hospital visits. The post Insurers Must Expand GP Coverage To Curb Rising Private Health Care Costs — PMPASKL appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: Aged Care Homes Struggle To Upgrade As Families Cannot Afford Higher Fees
items.summary: AgeCope president Delren Terrence Douglas says financial constraints, inconsistent local council rules and staff shortages make it difficult for aged care homes to upgrade. Families cannot afford monthly fees of RM3,000-RM5,000 but expect that standard of care, he says. The post Aged Care Homes Struggle To Upgrade As Families Cannot Afford Higher Fees appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: MMA Loses Moral Authority To Demand Vape Ban
items.summary: MMA has lost the moral high ground to demand a vape ban, unless it quits the Poisons Board to protest the Board’s endorsement of a proposed nicotine exemption. As an expert advisory body, the Poisons Board holds equal responsibility as the health minister. The post MMA Loses Moral Authority To Demand Vape Ban appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: Seniors Need Retirement Income Without Burdening Their Children: KALSIS
items.summary: Many seniors in Malaysia need steady income to fund retirement and health care while remaining independent in their own homes, rather than burdening their children. KALSIS proposes allowing them to unlock their properties’ value while retaining the right to live in them for life. The post Seniors Need Retirement Income Without Burdening Their Children: KALSIS appeared first on CodeBlue .

items.title: When New Glasses No Longer Help, The Problem May Be Keratoconus
items.summary: Keratoconus can cause progressive vision loss, often going undiagnosed in adolescents. A new procedure called CAIRS, available at Ara Damansara Medical Centre, uses donor corneal tissue to reshape the cornea and improve vision in selected patients. The post When New Glasses No Longer Help, The Problem May Be Keratoconus appeared first on CodeBlue .
